Author: Reich, David
Awards: Royal Society Science Book Prize, shortlist (2018)

Title: By Steppe, Desert, and Ocean: The Birth of Eurasia
Author: Cunliffe, Barry

Title: Mesopotamia: The Invention of the City
Author: Leick, Gwendolyn

Title: Gilgamesh: A New Translation of the Ancient Epic
Author: Helle, Sophus (trans.)
Notes: Helle's translation renders the Standard Babylonian version as continuous poetry, with five interpretive essays.

Title: Enheduana: The Complete Poems of the World's First Author
Author: Helle, Sophus (trans.)

Title: Enuma Elish: The Babylonian Epic of Creation
Author: Haubold, J.
Additional Authors: Helle, S., Jiménez, E., Wisnom, S. (eds.)
Notes: Confirmed: Bloomsbury Academic, Oct 2024, 352 pp paperback (xi + 337). Facing-page translation plus thirteen scholarly essays. Open access ebook also available.

Title: A History of the Ancient Near East, ca. 3000–323 BC
Author: Van De Mieroop, Marc

Title: From Cyrus to Alexander: A History of the Persian Empire
Author: Briant, Pierre
Notes: The standard reference work on the Achaemenid Empire. Long enough to function as a shelf in itself.

Title: The Histories
Author: Herodotus
Notes: The Landmark edition adds maps, appendices and running dates. Penguin's Marincola/de Sélincourt runs about 784 pp; Oxford's Waterfield about 800.

Title: The Iliad
Author: Homer
Notes: Lattimore's version runs about 608 pp, Lombardo's 608, Wilson's 848. Fagles is the common narrative-first choice.

Title: The Odyssey
Author: Homer
Notes: Emily Wilson's 2018 translation runs 592 pp and is the other obvious modern option.

Title: Ancient Greece: A History in Eleven Cities
Author: Cartledge, Paul

Title: The Peloponnesian War
Author: Kagan, Donald
Notes: The single-volume distillation of Kagan's four-volume study, which runs to roughly 1,800 pp.

Title: Oedipus the King and Antigone
Author: Sophocles
Notes: These two plays are rarely printed alone. The standard vehicle is The Three Theban Plays (432 pp), which adds Oedipus at Colonus; the two plays themselves run about 190 pp of it.

Title: From Alexander to Actium: The Historical Evolution of the Hellenistic Age
Author: Green, Peter

Title: The Beginnings of Rome: Italy and Rome from the Bronze Age to the Punic Wars
Author: Cornell, Timothy J.

Title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
Author: Beard, Mary

Title: Rubicon: The Last Years of the Roman Republic
Author: Holland, Tom

Title: The Aeneid
Author: Virgil
Notes: Fitzgerald's version runs 432 pp; Ruden's 2008 line-for-line translation about 320.

Title: The Fate of Rome: Climate, Disease, and the End of an Empire
Author: Harper, Kyle

Title: The Fall of the Roman Empire: A New History of Rome and the Barbarians
Author: Heather, Peter

Title: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
Author: Gibbon, Edward
Notes: Written and published in six volumes, and the complete text is still sold that way. Penguin's one-volume abridgement (ed. David Womersley) runs about 848 pp and cuts roughly three quarters of the text — a materially different reading experience, and worth deciding on deliberately. Component counts are the Everyman's Library set and are approximate.

Title: The World of Late Antiquity, AD 150–750
Author: Brown, Peter

Title: Byzantium: The Early Centuries
Author: Norwich, John Julius
Notes: Volume 1 of three. Volumes 2 and 3 are entry 6 in this section.

Title: De Administrando Imperio
Author: Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus
Notes: A scholarly Greek-and-English edition rather than a trade translation; harder to find and much drier than the rest of this section.

Title: Byzantium: The Apogee and Byzantium: The Decline and Fall
Author: Norwich, John Julius
Notes: This single line in the source list is two separate books, which is part of why the canon's own summary table undercounts this section.

Title: Cathedral, Forge, and Waterwheel: Technology and Invention in the Middle Ages
Author: Gies, Frances

Title: Feudal Society
Author: Bloch, Marc
Notes: Published in two volumes and usually sold that way in English; some printings bind both as one ~500 pp volume.

Title: The Hundred Years War I: Trial by Battle
Author: Sumption, Jonathan
Notes: First of five volumes; the completed sequence runs to roughly 4,000 pp. Only volume 1 is in the canon.

Title: Heart of Europe: A History of the Holy Roman Empire
Author: Wilson, Peter H.
Notes: Organised thematically rather than chronologically, which makes it the least narrative-first book in this section.

Title: Early China: A Social and Cultural History
Author: Feng, Li

Title: The Early Chinese Empires: Qin and Han
Author: Lewis, Mark Edward
Notes: The source list credits this to Dieter Kuhn. It is by Mark Edward Lewis; Kuhn wrote the Song volume, listed as entry 6 in this section. The two attributions appear to have been swapped.

Title: Three Kingdoms
Author: Luo, Guanzhong
Publisher: Foreign Languages Press / University of California Press
Notes: The unabridged Moss Roberts translation runs to four volumes. There is also a one-volume abridgement (~400 pp) that cuts about two thirds — a very different book. Component counts are approximate.

Title: China Between Empires: The Northern and Southern Dynasties
Author: Lewis, Mark Edward

Title: China's Cosmopolitan Empire: The Tang Dynasty
Author: Lewis, Mark Edward

Title: The Age of Confucian Rule: The Song Transformation of China
Author: Kuhn, Dieter
Notes: The source list credits this to Timothy Brook. It is by Dieter Kuhn; Brook wrote the Yuan/Ming volume, entry 7. See the note on entry 2 — the two are swapped.

Title: The Troubled Empire: China in the Yuan and Ming Dynasties
Author: Brook, Timothy

Title: The Story of the Stone
Author: Cao, Xueqin
Notes: Also known as Dream of the Red Chamber. Cao wrote the first eighty chapters; the last forty, translated by John Minford in volumes 4 and 5, are generally attributed to Gao E. Component counts are approximate.

Title: Kojiki: An Account of Ancient Matters
Author: Ō no Yasumaro (comp.)
Notes: The source list gives no author. The Kojiki was compiled by Ō no Yasumaro in 712. Donald Philippi's 1968 scholarly translation runs about 655 pp; Heldt's is the readable one.

Title: The Tale of Genji
Author: Murasaki Shikibu
Awards: PEN/Book-of-the-Month Club Translation Prize (2003) — Royall Tyler
Notes: Seidensticker's runs about 1,120 pp, Waley's abridged version about 1,136, Washburn's 2015 version about 1,344.

Title: The Tale of the Heike
Author: Anonymous
Notes: The source list gives the author as 'YUKINAGA, Shōbutsu', which merges two names from the traditional attribution — the monk Yukinaga as compiler and the biwa player Shōbutsu as performer. The work is effectively anonymous.

Title: Emperor of Japan: Meiji and His World, 1852–1912
Author: Keene, Donald

Title: Embracing Defeat: Japan in the Wake of World War II
Author: Dower, John W.
Awards: Pulitzer Prize for General Non-Fiction (1999); National Book Award for Nonfiction (1999); Bancroft Prize (2000)

Title: A Concise History of Korea, Volumes I–II
Author: Seth, Michael J.
Notes: Confirmed as a two-volume set: a premodern volume and a modern one. Rowman also publishes a single-volume A Concise History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (2nd ed. 2016, 626 pp; 3rd ed. 2019, 612 pp) covering the same ground — worth checking which one you actually want.

Title: The Imjin War: Japan's Sixteenth-Century Invasion of Korea and Attempt to Conquer China
Author: Hawley, Samuel

Title: The Memoirs of Lady Hyegyŏng
Author: Lady Hyegyŏng
Notes: The source list renders the author as 'HŎNG SŎK-HYEGYŎNGGUNG', which is garbled. She is Lady Hyegyŏng (Hyegyŏnggung Hong Ssi), crown princess of Chosŏn.

Title: The Story of Hong Gildong
Author: Kang, Minsoo (trans./ed.)
Notes: The shortest book in the canon.

Title: Ancient China and Its Enemies: The Rise of Nomadic Power in East Asian History
Author: Di Cosmo, Nicola

Title: The Perilous Frontier: Nomadic Empires and China, 221 BC to AD 1757
Author: Barfield, Thomas J.

Title: The Tibetan Empire in Central Asia
Author: Beckwith, Christopher I.

Title: The Reconquest of Spain
Author: Lomax, Derek W.
Notes: Long out of print and hard to find; the most likely gap in this section.

Title: The Quest for El Cid
Author: Fletcher, Richard
Awards: Wolfson History Prize (1989); Los Angeles Times Book Prize, History (1990)

Title: The Cid and His Spain
Author: Menéndez Pidal, Ramón
Notes: The source list files this under 'PIDAL' — the surname is Menéndez Pidal.

Title: The Conquest of New Spain
Author: Díaz del Castillo, Bernal
Notes: Cohen's Penguin text is abridged. Janet Burke and Ted Humphrey's 2012 Hackett translation is fuller at about 528 pp.

Title: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle
Author: Anonymous
Notes: A composite of several manuscript recensions rather than a single text; Swanton prints them in parallel.

Title: Foundation: The History of England from Its Earliest Beginnings to the Tudors
Author: Ackroyd, Peter
Notes: First of six volumes; only this one is in the canon.

Title: The Sinews of Power: War, Money and the English State, 1688–1783
Author: Brewer, John

Title: Chronicles
Author: Froissart, Jean
Notes: Heavily abridged. The complete Chronicles run to several thousand pages and have no modern full English edition.

Title: Memoirs: The Reign of Louis XI, 1461–83
Author: Commynes, Philippe de

Title: The Old Regime and the French Revolution
Author: Tocqueville, Alexis de
Notes: The University of Chicago's Alan Kahan translation is a two-volume scholarly edition; the Anchor one-volume is the reading edition.

Title: Citizens: A Chronicle of the French Revolution
Author: Schama, Simon

Title: A History of the American People
Author: Johnson, Paul
Notes: Openly polemical and the most ideologically committed book in the canon; useful to read against Bailyn and McPherson rather than alone.

Title: Battle Cry of Freedom: The Civil War Era
Author: McPherson, James M.
Awards: Pulitzer Prize for History (1989)

Title: Personal Memoirs
Author: Grant, Ulysses S.
Notes: Originally two volumes. Modern one-volume editions (Penguin Classics, Library of America) run about 800 pp; the Library of America text adds Grant's selected letters and runs to roughly 1,200.

Title: The Ideological Origins of the American Revolution
Author: Bailyn, Bernard
Awards: Pulitzer Prize for History (1968); Bancroft Prize (1968)

Title: Europe: The Struggle for Supremacy, 1453 to the Present
Author: Simms, Brendan
